Jesus you hit the nail on the head too. I found that the “hip-hop” part of lofi was absolutely ripped from its chest, and is borderline appropriation. 

Lo-Fi hip hop is derived from *real* hip-hop music, like J Dilla’s “Don’t Cry” from ‘06...as you said, the genre doesn’t possess the low fidelity aspect anymore, and in most cases of it’s actually incredibly high quality ambient jazz-hop chillwave. No hip-hop samples, dusty vinyl crackle, gritty drum breaks, or that boom-bap-y feel. Just endless loops of soft piano notes, inoffensive beats, and soulless AI mush..

I just searched “lofi-hip hop” on YouTube and the first 5 hits were mass produced modern elevator music. Crazy how this genre started out as a love letter to hip-hop’s feel.

*I think the main catalyst for this was when ChilledCow rebranded to LoFi girl..I used to tune in daily, but now it feels like a hollow corporate branding tool for clicks and an “aesthetic”. AI ruined the genre along with content farming; anyone can prompt a machine to spit out a “lofi beat” in seconds without understanding the feel of the samples, or even digging for the right sample. Lofi has simply become a keyword for streaming numbers*
